alBiruni_1029_Wright1934.note: Five-way Arabic scheme, NOT the Latin four-way one. Codes: b = brilliant (nayyir), l = luminous (mudi'), d = dusky (qutmah), m = the typed symbol that the legend glosses "dark or shadowed (muzlim)" (typed like an s), v = empty (khali). The run lengths often coincide with the Latin runs but the labels do not map one-to-one (see SOURCES.md). Aquarius last cell has a handwritten mark beside L5 in the typescript.

Lilly_London_1647.note: Codes: L = lucidus/light, D = tenebrosus/dark, S = fumosus/smoky, V = vacuus/void. raw = Lilly's letter.end-degree notation (d/l/sm/v); "f" stands for the long-s abbreviation printed in Capricorn (s.15), read as smoky (the run length matches Alcabitius fu 5). Virgo "v.27": the letter is poorly inked; read as v (matches Alcabitius va 5).

Alcabitius_Venice_1482_Ratdolt.note: P = pitted (puteus). Fixed five-column table: six-entry signs of the later printings are cut to five (Leo 28, Sagittarius 30, Capricorn 7, Aquarius 24 absent); Libra has an extra 21; Scorpio has a blank cell.

Alcabitius_Venice_1485_Ratdolt_Saxonia.note: P = pitted (puteus). Taurus and Libra rows have one blank cell each, as printed.

Bonatti_Augsburg_1491_Ratdolt.note: P = pitted. Venice 1506 identical (incl. Aquarius 11 and no Sagittarius 30).

Alcabitius_Venice_1482_Ratdolt_as_printe.note: UNRELIABLE. What this printing sets under the azemena heading is, sign by sign, a corrupt copy of the degrees-increasing-fortune list (compare Gemini 11, Libra 3 5 21, Aquarius 7 16 17 20, Sagittarius 13 20); the azemena numbers appear instead under the fortune heading (see increasing_fortune). Kept only to record the printing.
